author: N. T. Foster
title: Senate approves Smith bill allowing safety cables for towing vehicles in Pennsylvania
text:
← Back to the wire
Senate approves Smith bill allowing safety cables for towing vehicles in Pennsylvania
The Senate has unanimously approved legislation by Representative Brian Smith permitting the use of safety cables instead of only chains when towing vehicles in Pennsylvania. The bill now awaits action by the governor before becoming law.
The Senate unanimously approved legislation sponsored by State Representative Brian Smith to allow the use of safety cables when towing vehicles, according to an Oct. 7 announcement.
Current law requires the use of safety chains when two vehicles are connected by certain hitches or devices, aiming to prevent the tow bar from hitting the ground if it fails or becomes disconnected. The new legislation would permit drivers to use safety cables as an alternative. "While safety chains get the job done, safety cables are lighter and easier to handle, while being just as strong and capable as conventional chains," Smith said. "Owning a transportation company for two decades has taught me that cables take up far less space and last longer than safety chains. While chains will still be permitted, we should give Pennsylvanians the choice to take advantage of this tool."
House Bill 71 now heads to the governor’s desk for signature before it can become law. Smith said, "As legislators, it’s our job to listen to our constituents’ issues, and come to Harrisburg to try to fix them. While there are many things that still need fixing, I’m glad to be able to get this done. We’re one step away from preventing any more tickets being written over this."
Smith has experience in transportation business ownership through Fastrak Inc., Orion Logistics Inc., and co-ownership of Abacus Housing LLC; he also studied business and accounting at Penn State University, according to his official website. He resided in Punxsutawney with his wife Linda and children Jake, Jadie and Josh; he held seats on several legislative committees including Liquor Control; Tourism, Recreation and Economic Development; Game and Fisheries; Transportation; chaired subcommittees on Aviation within Transportation Committee and Recreation within Tourism Committee; served on Pennsylvania Infrastructure Investment Authority board as well as Legislative Budget and Finance Committee—all according to his official website.
